intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Historic Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over 1,500 years, followed by a visit to the stunning Sultan Ahmed Mosque (Blue Mosque) with its six minarets and exquisite Iznik tile interior. Hire a local guide for deep historical context.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Bazaar Exploration
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops, then head to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar to sample Turkish delight, saffron, dried fruits, and aromatic spices. Engage with local vendors and practice the art of bargaining.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a local home or boutique culinary school where you'll learn to prepare classic Ottoman and Turkish dishes such as meze, börek, lamb kebabs, and baklava. Includes a market visit to source fresh ingredients and a communal meal at the end.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Archaeology Museums Day
experiences.description: Spend a full day at Topkapi Palace, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years, exploring its treasury, harem, and imperial kitchens. Continue to the adjacent Istanbul Archaeology Museums to view artifacts spanning 5,000 years of Anatolian and Mediterranean civilizations.

experiences.name: Bosphorus Sunset Cruise & Waterfront Meyhane Dinner
experiences.description: Take a scenic public ferry cruise along the Bosphorus Strait, passing Ottoman palaces, yalıs (wooden mansions), and the iconic bridges connecting Europe and Asia. End the evening at a traditional meyhane (Turkish tavern) in Karaköy for a feast of meze, fresh fish, and rakı, experiencing authentic Istanbul nightlife.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the Havaist airport bus or metro to central Istanbul for a budget-friendly transfer (approx. 30-50 TRY). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Settle into your room and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack from a 24-hour street stall or convenience store near the hotel — try a simit (sesame bread ring) or a döner wrap for under 50 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Turkish Lira (TRY) ready for the airport transfer. The Havaist bus is the cheapest option from Istanbul Airport. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements in advance since arrival is late night.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel or a nearby local kahvaltı (Turkish breakfast) café. Take a slow morning walk along the beachfront area to get oriented with the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest local bazaar or neighborhood market on foot. Pick up fresh fruits, olives, and local snacks. Visit a nearby mosque or historic neighborhood landmark to ease into Istanbul's culture without overwhelming yourself on day one.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the waterfront at sunset. Find a local meyhane (tavern) or casual eatery for a relaxed first dinner in Istanbul. Try classic dishes like mercimek çorbası (lentil soup) and pide bread.

meals.breakfast: Local kahvaltı café near the hotel — full Turkish breakfast spread with cheese, olives, eggs, tomatoes for 80-120 TRY
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit and simit from a street vendor or local bakery — under 40 TRY
meals.dinner: Neighborhood lokanta (casual Turkish restaurant) — lentil soup, pide, and ayran for 100-150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to get your bearings. Download the Istanbul public transit app (Istanbul Kart) and purchase an Istanbul Kart for cheap tram, metro, and ferry rides throughout your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Take the tram or ferry to Sultanahmet (Old City). Visit the iconic Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — entry is free as it is now an active mosque. Dress modestly and bring a scarf. Spend 1.5-2 hours marveling at the Byzantine and Ottoman architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 5 minutes to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) — also free to enter. Then explore the Hippodrome of Constantinople and its ancient obelisks. Stroll through the Sultanahmet Square area and visit the Basilica Cistern (entry approx. 200 TRY) — an underground Byzantine water reservoir with atmospheric lighting.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Arasta Bazaar near the Blue Mosque for budget souvenir shopping. Enjoy dinner in Sultanahmet at a local spot away from the main tourist strip to avoid inflated prices.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a börek (savory pastry) from a local bakkal (corner shop) for 30-50 TRY
meals.lunch: Gözleme (stuffed flatbread) from a street stall in Sultanahmet — 60-80 TRY
meals.dinner: Local kebab restaurant in Sultanahmet side streets — adana kebab plate with salad and bread for 150-200 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Hagia Sophia and Blue Mosque are free but require modest dress (shoulders and knees covered, shoes removed). Visit early morning to avoid crowds. Basilica Cistern is worth the entry fee for history lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapi Palace (entry approx. 500-600 TRY — book online to save time). Explore the sprawling complex that served as the heart of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years. See the Imperial Treasury, the Harem (additional fee), and stunning Bosphorus views from the palace gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill to Gülhane Park — one of Istanbul's oldest and largest parks, free to enter. Relax on the grass, enjoy the greenery, and soak in views over the Bosphorus. Nearby, visit the Istanbul Archaeology Museums (approx. 200 TRY) — home to artifacts from across the ancient world.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Eminönü waterfront. Watch the famous balık-ekmek (fish sandwich) boats and grab one for a cheap and iconic Istanbul meal. Watch the sunset over the Golden Horn from Galata Bridge.

meals.breakfast: Simits and tea from a street cart near the hotel or tram stop — 20-30 TRY
meals.lunch: Packed snacks from a bakery or a quick pide from a lokanta near Topkapi — 80-120 TRY
meals.dinner: Balık-ekmek (fish sandwich) from the floating boats at Eminönü — 80-100 TRY, plus a glass of şalgam (turnip juice) for 20 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is large — wear comfortable shoes. The Harem is a separate ticket but highly recommended for history enthusiasts. Arrive at opening time (9:00 AM) to beat tour groups.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets, free to enter. Browse over 4,000 shops selling spices, ceramics, jewelry, textiles, and leather goods. Practice your bargaining skills — never pay the first price.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to the Egyptian Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı / Spice Bazaar) — another free-to-enter historic market. Buy Turkish spices, dried fruits, lokum (Turkish delight), and nuts as gifts or snacks. Explore the surrounding Eminönü neighborhood streets.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Galata Bridge on foot and climb up to the Galata Tower neighborhood (Karaköy). Walk the bohemian streets of Karaköy and enjoy the street art and independent cafés.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at a local café in your neighborhood — 80-120 TRY
meals.lunch: Kumpir (stuffed baked potato) from a street vendor near the Bazaars — 80-100 TRY
meals.dinner: Casual meyhane in Karaköy — meze plates (hummus, ezme, haydari) with bread and a soft drink for 150-200 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Plan accordingly. Bargaining is expected and part of the culture — start at 50-60% of the asking price. Keep small bills handy.

day_by_day.morning: Take the tram to Beyoğlu and walk up İstiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi) — Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard stretching 1.4 km. Observe the stunning 19th-century European-style architecture, art nouveau buildings, and the historic red tram that runs its length.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Galata Tower (entry approx. 300 TRY) for panoramic 360-degree views over Istanbul and the Bosphorus. Then explore the narrow cobblestone streets of the Galata neighborhood below. Visit the Galata Mevlevi Lodge Museum (approx. 100 TRY) to learn about Sufi whirling dervish culture.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the vibrant nightlife atmosphere of İstiklal and Beyoğlu without spending much — street musicians, performers, and free cultural energy abound. Find a budget meyhane for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Börek from a pastane (pastry shop) on İstiklal — 40-60 TRY with tea
meals.lunch: Tantuni wrap or lahmacun (thin flatbread with minced meat) from a street stall — 60-80 TRY
meals.dinner: Beyoğlu meyhane — grilled fish or köfte plate with salad for 180-220 TRY

day_by_day.notes: İstiklal Avenue is very busy on weekends. The historic red tram on İstiklal is a fun and cheap ride. The Galata area is hilly — wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take a public ferry (Istanbul Kart — approx. 25 TRY) across the Bosphorus to the Asian side of Istanbul. Arrive at Kadıköy — a vibrant, trendy neighborhood beloved by locals. Explore the Kadıköy Market (Tarihi Kadıköy Çarşısı) with its fresh produce, fish, cheese, and spice vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Moda neighborhood — a charming seaside district with tree-lined streets, independent cafés, and beautiful Bosphorus views. Visit Moda Park and relax by the sea. Browse the independent bookshops and vintage stores on Moda Caddesi.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Kadıköy — the Asian side is known for excellent, authentic, and affordable food. Return to the European side by ferry at night for beautiful illuminated Bosphorus views.

meals.breakfast: On the ferry or grab a simit and tea at the Kadıköy ferry dock — 25-30 TRY
meals.lunch: Fresh fish sandwich or kokoreç (offal sandwich) from Kadıköy Market street stalls — 80-100 TRY
meals.dinner: Kadıköy lokanta — home-style Turkish dishes like kuru fasulye (bean stew) and rice for 120-160 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Bosphorus ferry is one of Istanbul's great budget experiences — beautiful views for the price of a transit card tap. Kadıköy is considered more local and less touristy than the European side — embrace it.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably Istanbul's most beautiful mosque and a masterpiece by architect Mimar Sinan. Free to enter. The mosque sits on a hilltop with sweeping views over the Golden Horn. Explore the surrounding Süleymaniye neighborhood with its traditional Ottoman-era streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill to the Vefa neighborhood and visit the historic Vefa Bozacısı — a legendary shop selling boza (a traditional fermented drink) since 1876. Continue to the Zeyrek neighborhood and explore the Church of the Pantocrator (Zeyrek Mosque) — a stunning Byzantine monument, free or small donation.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Fener and Balat neighborhoods — among Istanbul's most atmospheric and photogenic areas with colorful houses, Greek and Jewish heritage, and antique shops.

meals.breakfast: Neighborhood bakery near the hotel — cheese toast and tea for 50-70 TRY
meals.lunch: Soup kitchen (aşevi) near Süleymaniye Mosque — traditional Turkish soups and stews for 80-120 TRY
meals.dinner: Balat neighborhood café or small restaurant — meze and bread for 150-180 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Süleymaniye Mosque has a beautiful garden and courtyard — great for photography. Boza is an acquired taste but worth trying for the cultural experience. Balat is very photogenic — bring your camera.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Chora Church (Kariye Museum / Chora Mosque) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — famous for its extraordinarily well-preserved Byzantine mosaics and frescoes (entry approx. 200 TRY). One of the finest examples of Byzantine art in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Walls — the 5th-century defensive walls that protected Constantinople for over 1,000 years. Stretch for nearly 7 km and are largely free to explore. Head to the Eyüp Sultan neighborhood and visit the Eyüp Sultan Mosque — one of the holiest sites in Istanbul, free to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Pierre Loti Cable Car (teleferik) up to the Pierre Loti Hill Café for panoramic views over the Golden Horn at sunset — cable car approx. 20-30 TRY. Enjoy tea at the historic hilltop café.

meals.breakfast: Simit and boiled eggs from a street cart — 30-40 TRY
meals.lunch: Pide or lahmacun from a local fırın (oven bakery) in Edirnekapı — 80-100 TRY
meals.dinner: Eyüp neighborhood restaurant — Ottoman-style lamb dishes or kebab for 160-200 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Eyüp Sultan Mosque is a deeply sacred site — dress very modestly and be respectful. The Pierre Loti Cable Car runs regularly and the hilltop views are spectacular, especially at golden hour.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longer Bosphorus ferry cruise — purchase a public ferry ticket (approx. 50-80 TRY) for the scenic commuter ferry that runs up the Bosphorus, passing palaces, fortresses, and fishing villages. Get off at Anadolu Kavağı (the last stop) on the Asian side.
day_by_day.afternoon: Climb up to Yoros Castle (Genoese Castle) above Anadolu Kavağı — free to enter, with stunning views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Explore the small fishing village below. Take the return ferry back toward the city.
day_by_day.evening: Disembark at Beşiktaş or Ortaköy on the return. Visit the ornate Ortaköy Mosque right on the Bosphorus waterfront. Try the famous Ortaköy kumpir (giant stuffed baked potato) — a local institution.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab food at the ferry terminal — 60-80 TRY
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at a waterfront restaurant in Anadolu Kavağı — 150-200 TRY (splurge-worthy for the setting)
meals.dinner: Ortaköy kumpir (stuffed baked potato) with all toppings — 100-120 TRY, eat by the Bosphorus

day_by_day.notes: The Bosphorus public ferry is a budget traveler's dream — same views as expensive tourist cruises at a fraction of the cost. Check ferry schedules in advance as they run a few times per day. Bring a light jacket for the ferry.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace (entry approx. 500-600 TRY) — the lavish 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus shore in Beşiktaş. Guided tours only (included in ticket). Home to the largest chandelier in the world and Atatürk's bedroom where he died in 1938.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to Yıldız Park — a large, beautiful forested park on a hillside above Beşiktaş, free to enter. Explore the park's pavilions and enjoy the peaceful green escape. Visit the small Yıldız Porcelain Factory Museum if open.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Beşiktaş neighborhood for dinner — a lively, authentic local district popular with students and young Istanbulites. Explore the Beşiktaş fish market area.

meals.breakfast: Pastane (pastry café) near the hotel — menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes) for 80-100 TRY
meals.lunch: Packed snacks from a bakery or grab a döner from a Beşiktaş street stall — 80-100 TRY
meals.dinner: Beşiktaş meyhane or lokanta — grilled köfte and salad for 160-200 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace tours are timed — book ahead or arrive early. Photography is restricted inside. The palace is genuinely jaw-dropping even for budget travelers — worth the splurge.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a public ferry from Kabataş terminal (approx. 50-80 TRY each way) to Büyükada, the largest of the nine islands in the Sea of Marmara. No cars are allowed — only horse-drawn carriages and bicycles. Rent a bicycle (approx. 100-150 TRY for a few hours) and explore the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or walk to Aya Yorgi (St. George) Monastery on the hilltop of Büyükada — stunning views over the Sea of Marmara and the Istanbul skyline in the distance. Explore the island's Victorian-era wooden mansions and quiet streets.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Istanbul at sunset — the views of the city skyline from the sea are unforgettable. Enjoy a final relaxed dinner back in your neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the ferry terminal or hotel — 60-80 TRY
meals.lunch: Seafood meze and fresh fish at a Büyükada waterfront restaurant — 200-250 TRY (island dining is a slight splurge but worth it)
meals.dinner: Budget lokanta near the hotel — home-cooked Turkish food for 120-160 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Büyükada is magical and peaceful — a total contrast to Istanbul's urban intensity. Ferries run regularly. The island gets busy on weekends — arrive early. Bring sunscreen and water for the hilltop hike.

day_by_day.morning: Revisit any favorite spots or neighborhoods you want to see one last time. Head back to the Grand Bazaar or Spice Bazaar for any last-minute gift shopping. Pick up Turkish tea, spices, lokum, and small ceramics as affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Istanbul Modern (İstanbul Modern Sanat Müzesi) — Turkey's leading contemporary art museum on the Bosphorus waterfront in Karaköy (entry approx. 200-250 TRY). A great final cultural experience. Enjoy the Bosphorus views from the museum café.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant discovered during the trip. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. If flying out the next day, confirm transfer arrangements. If departing tonight, head to the airport via Havaist bus or metro.

meals.breakfast: Final full Turkish breakfast at a neighborhood kahvaltı café — 100-130 TRY (treat yourself)
meals.lunch: Casual street food in Karaköy near Istanbul Modern — balık sandwich or gözleme for 80-100 TRY
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your favorite lokanta or kebab house from the trip — budget 200-250 TRY for a celebratory final meal

day_by_day.notes: Keep airport transfer time in mind — Istanbul Airport is about 45-60 minutes from the city center by Havaist bus. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Use remaining TRY on food and small souvenirs as currency exchange back can be costly.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the hotel or a nearby 24-hour lokanta (Turkish diner) — try a bowl of mercimek çorbası (lentil soup) and bread to ease into Turkish cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Pre-arrange airport transfer to avoid stress. Exchange some currency or use an ATM at the airport for initial expenses. Rest well — big days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start at the hotel. Enjoy breakfast and take a short orientation walk along the beachfront promenade near Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings. Breathe in the sea air and acclimate to Istanbul's rhythm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the historic Sultanahmet district (approx. 30–45 min by tram/taxi). Visit the iconic Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — marvel at its Byzantine mosaics, Ottoman minarets, and layered history spanning nearly 1,500 years. Explore at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll across Sultanahmet Square to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque). Admire its stunning exterior and six minarets at dusk. Wander the nearby Arasta Bazaar for a relaxed first shopping browse.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet — enjoy Turkish staples like beyaz peynir (white cheese), olives, tomatoes, cucumbers, simit, and çay (tea).
meals.lunch: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — a legendary spot near Sultanahmet serving classic köfte (grilled meatballs) with white beans and bread at mid-range prices.
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant near the Sultanahmet area — Ottoman-inspired cuisine in a historic setting; try lamb dishes and Ottoman pilaf.

day_by_day.notes: Hagia Sophia is free to enter but may require modest dress (head covering for women available at entrance). Arrive early afternoon to beat crowds. Comfortable walking shoes essential.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapi Palace — the grand seat of the Ottoman Empire for over 400 years. Explore the Imperial Treasury, Harem quarters, and stunning panoramic views over the Bosphorus and Golden Horn. Allocate at least 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Istanbul Archaeological Museums — one of the world's great archaeology collections housing the Alexander Sarcophagus, ancient Anatolian artifacts, and the Museum of the Ancient Orient. A hidden gem often overlooked by tourists.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Galata Bridge area. Walk across the bridge lined with fishermen, then explore the lively Karaköy neighborhood below for waterfront ambiance and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Konyalı Restaurant inside Topkapi Palace grounds — historic and atmospheric, serving traditional Turkish dishes; mid-range pricing.
meals.dinner: Karaköy Lokantası in Karaköy — beloved neighborhood restaurant known for traditional Turkish home cooking, mezes, and fresh fish; excellent value.

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace entry fee applies; Harem has a separate ticket. Book Harem entry in advance or arrive early as slots fill quickly. The Archaeological Museums are underrated — budget 1.5 hours minimum.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Browse carpets, ceramics, spices, jewelry, and leather goods. Practice your bargaining skills!
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü. Sample Turkish delight, dried fruits, nuts, saffron, and local teas. Pick up food souvenirs. Afterward, visit the nearby Rüstem Pasha Mosque — a masterpiece of Iznik tile work, often less crowded.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short ferry from Eminönü to Üsküdar on the Asian side of Istanbul — a memorable 15-minute Bosphorus crossing. Stroll the Asian shore, visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque, and enjoy the European skyline from the other side.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pandeli Restaurant above the Spice Bazaar entrance — a classic Istanbul institution with Ottoman-era décor; try their stuffed mussels and lamb dishes.
meals.dinner: Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy (accessible by ferry from Üsküdar) — famous for authentic Anatolian regional dishes; a must-visit for food lovers. Very affordable.

day_by_day.notes: Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays — check if applicable. Carry small bills for bazaar purchases. The Üsküdar ferry costs just a few lira and is an experience in itself. Kadıköy is a vibrant foodie neighborhood worth exploring.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — an atmospheric underground Byzantine water reservoir with dramatic columns, mood lighting, and the famous Medusa head bases. Spend about an hour exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk uphill to explore the Hippodrome of Constantinople — the ancient chariot-racing stadium. See the Egyptian Obelisk, Serpent Column, and German Fountain. Then visit the Ibrahim Pasha Palace housing the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.
day_by_day.evening: Take a tram to Beyoğlu and walk up the iconic İstiklal Avenue (Independence Avenue) — a 1.4km pedestrian boulevard buzzing with shops, cafés, street performers, and historic buildings. Ride the nostalgic red tram along the avenue.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Hafız Mustafa 1864 near Sultanahmet — iconic Turkish patisserie and café; try börek, baklava, and Turkish coffee for a light but authentic lunch.
meals.dinner: Zübeyir Ocakbaşı on Bekar Sokak near İstiklal — legendary grill restaurant with open charcoal hearth; exceptional kebabs and mezes in a lively atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Basilica Cistern recently renovated with enhanced lighting — very photogenic. Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts has outstanding carpet and calligraphy collections. İstiklal Avenue is busiest in the evening — embrace the energy.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Bosphorus cruise — book a public ferry (şehir hatları) from Eminönü for a budget-friendly full Bosphorus tour passing yalıs (waterfront mansions), Rumeli Fortress, Dolmabahçe Palace, and the two Bosphorus bridges. A 90-minute scenic journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Anadolu Kavağı (the final stop on the full Bosphorus tour) on the Asian shore. Climb up to the medieval Yoros Castle for panoramic views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Explore the charming fishing village.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Eminönü. Head to Karaköy or Galata neighborhood. Climb the historic Galata Tower for 360-degree panoramic views of Istanbul at dusk — spectacular golden hour photography opportunity.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at one of the seaside restaurants in Anadolu Kavağı village — try levrek (sea bass) or çipura (sea bream) with meze; very fresh and mid-range priced.
meals.dinner: Galata area — Lokanta Maya in Karaköy; innovative modern Turkish cuisine using seasonal local ingredients in a warm, intimate setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book the full Bosphorus public ferry early morning at Eminönü docks (departures limited). The Yoros Castle hike is moderate — wear comfortable shoes. Galata Tower has an entry fee; go 30 minutes before sunset for best light.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Dolmabahçe Palace — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman imperial palace on the European Bosphorus shore. Guided tours of the ceremonial halls, crystal staircase, and the room where Atatürk passed away. Stunning blend of Ottoman and European Baroque architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Beşiktaş waterfront to Yıldız Park — a forested hillside park with Ottoman pavilions, a small lake, and peaceful walking paths. Visit Yıldız Palace Museum within the park grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the trendy Beşiktaş or Ortaköy neighborhoods. Visit the photogenic Ortaköy Mosque beside the Bosphorus Bridge. Browse the Ortaköy craft market (weekends especially lively) and enjoy the vibrant waterfront square.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Sunset Café in Yıldız Park — pleasant outdoor café within the park; sandwiches, Turkish tea, and light bites in a serene green setting.
meals.dinner: Banyan Restaurant in Ortaköy — stylish waterfront Asian-fusion restaurant with Bosphorus Bridge views; splurge-worthy mid-range dinner with cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires timed entry tickets — book online in advance. Photography restrictions inside the palace. Ortaköy is famous for kumpir (giant stuffed baked potatoes) — grab one as a street food snack in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — home to some of the finest surviving Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, depicting the life of Christ and the Virgin Mary. A UNESCO World Heritage treasure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Land Walls — the 5th-century Byzantine fortifications stretching 6.5km across the peninsula. Explore the Edirnekapı gate section, climb sections of the walls, and photograph the towers. Visit the nearby Blachernae Palace ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Istanbul. Explore the Fener and Balat neighborhoods — colorful historic districts with Greek Orthodox and Jewish heritage, charming painted houses, antique shops, and authentic local cafés.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Asitane Restaurant near Chora Church — acclaimed restaurant serving recreated Ottoman palace recipes from historical sources; unique cultural dining experience.
meals.dinner: Forno Balat in Balat neighborhood — beloved local spot for wood-fired bread, mezes, and hearty Turkish home cooking in a colorful neighborhood setting.

day_by_day.notes: Chora Church/Kariye Mosque may have restricted access depending on prayer schedules — check current status before visiting. Balat is a photographer's paradise — bring your camera. This area is less touristy and gives a genuine neighborhood feel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — Sinan's masterpiece and arguably Istanbul's most architecturally significant Ottoman mosque. Explore the mosque, its courtyard, the tombs of Suleiman the Magnificent and Roxelana, and the surrounding külliye (mosque complex).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Tahtakale and Mahmutpaşa neighborhoods below Süleymaniye — authentic local wholesale markets selling fabrics, spices, and everyday goods. Experience Istanbul as locals live it, far from tourist crowds. Visit the nearby Beyazıt Square and Istanbul University gate.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Cihangir neighborhood in Beyoğlu — a bohemian, artistic district beloved by Istanbul's creative community. Browse independent bookshops, art galleries, and vintage stores. Enjoy the relaxed café culture.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Tarihi Süleymaniye Kurufasülyecisi — a legendary 80-year-old restaurant near Süleymaniye serving kuru fasülye (white bean stew) with rice and pickles; simple, delicious, and very affordable.
meals.dinner: Cihangir neighborhood — Sabiha'nın Yeri or a local meyhane (tavern); enjoy rakı with cold mezes, grilled fish, and live fasıl music for a quintessential Istanbul evening.

day_by_day.notes: Süleymaniye Mosque is less crowded than the Blue Mosque and arguably more beautiful — don't miss it. Mahmutpaşa market is a sensory overload in the best way. Meyhane culture is central to Istanbul social life — embrace it.

day_by_day.morning: Experience a traditional Turkish hammam (bathhouse). Visit Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584) or Çağaloğlu Hamamı (built 1741) — both historic 16th/18th century bathhouses offering the full kese (exfoliation) and köpük (foam massage) treatment. A rejuvenating cultural ritual.
day_by_day.afternoon: Refreshed and relaxed, explore the Kapalıçarşı area more deeply — visit the Nuruosmaniye Mosque adjacent to the bazaar, a rare Ottoman Baroque masterpiece. Browse the antique dealers on Çarşıkapı Street for Ottoman-era objects, coins, and curiosities.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Nişantaşı neighborhood — Istanbul's upscale fashion district. Window-shop designer boutiques, explore the tree-lined streets, and enjoy the sophisticated European atmosphere of this elegant residential quarter.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Köşkeroğlu Baklava & Restaurant near the Grand Bazaar — excellent Turkish home cooking followed by world-class pistachio baklava; mid-range and satisfying.
meals.dinner: Nişantaşı — Kantin Restaurant; beloved neighborhood restaurant serving modern Turkish bistro food with seasonal ingredients; popular with Istanbul's creative professionals.

day_by_day.notes: Hammam visit costs approximately 300–600 TL depending on package — book in advance online. Bring flip-flops and a change of clothes. Tip the tellak (bath attendant) generously. Nişantaşı is a pleasant contrast to the historic districts — very local and chic.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a ferry from Kabataş or Bostancı to Büyükada, the largest island. No motorized vehicles allowed — rent a bicycle or take a horse-drawn carriage. Explore Victorian-era wooden mansions, pine forests, and hilltop monasteries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Büyükada — hike or ride up to the Monastery of Saint George on the hilltop for sweeping Marmara Sea views. Swim at one of the small beaches (weather permitting in May). Enjoy the peaceful, car-free atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul (approximately 1.5 hours). Arrive back in the city energized. Head to the Kadıköy Asian side neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most vibrant and youthful districts with excellent street food, bars, and a lively night market.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a simit and tea from a street vendor at the ferry terminal.
meals.lunch: Buyukada Ocakbaşı on the island — fresh fish and grilled meats with Marmara Sea views; iconic island dining experience.
meals.dinner: Kadıköy food market street (Moda/Bahariye area) — graze on kokoreç (offal sandwich), midye dolma (stuffed mussels), balık ekmek (fish sandwich), and fresh pomegranate juice from street vendors.

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance — Büyükada ferries run regularly but can be crowded on weekends. Bicycle rental on the island costs approximately 100–150 TL/hour. Bring sunscreen and a light jacket for the ferry. Kadıköy is perfect for a relaxed, local evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) on the Bosphorus waterfront in Karaköy — Turkey's premier contemporary art museum housed in a stunning Renzo Piano-designed building. Explore Turkish modern art, photography exhibitions, and temporary shows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the SALT Galata cultural center in the historic Ottoman Bank building — free exhibitions on architecture, urban history, and contemporary culture. Then walk through the atmospheric Galata neighborhood, visiting the Galata Mevlevi Lodge (Whirling Dervish museum) for Sufi history.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Sema ceremony — the mystical Whirling Dervish ritual performed by Mevlevi Sufis. Several venues in Istanbul offer authentic performances including Hodjapasha Cultural Center near Sirkeci. A deeply moving and culturally significant experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Müzedechanga at Istanbul Modern — the museum's acclaimed restaurant with stunning Bosphorus views; modern Turkish cuisine with international influences; worth the splurge.
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner at Hocapaşa area near Sirkeci — Hamdi Restaurant; rooftop terrace with Golden Horn views, excellent southeastern Turkish kebabs and mezes.

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Modern entry fee applies. Book Whirling Dervish Sema ceremony tickets in advance — performances sell out, especially at Hodjapasha. The ceremony lasts approximately 1 hour and is a profound cultural highlight of any Istanbul visit.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — return to any favorite spots or explore areas you missed. Consider visiting the Pierre Loti Café on a hilltop in Eyüp (accessible by cable car) for panoramic Golden Horn views and tea — a beloved Istanbul tradition. Or revisit Sultanahmet for final photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping — return to the Grand Bazaar or Spice Bazaar for final purchases. Pick up Turkish tea sets, hand-painted ceramics, evil eye (nazar boncuğu) charms, or premium Turkish delight. Pack thoughtfully.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner celebrating 13 days in Istanbul. Transfer to airport or continue stay based on your onward travel plans.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — savor the full Turkish spread one last time.
meals.lunch: Eyüp Sultan area — Café Pierre Loti for tea and light bites with Golden Horn panorama, or a local pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) restaurant near the mosque.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Assk Cafe in Ortaköy or a classic Sultanahmet restaurant — toast to Istanbul with a glass of Turkish wine or ayran and a full Ottoman feast: mezes, kebabs, and baklava for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–3.5 hours before your departure flight for airport transfer and check-in. Istanbul traffic can be unpredictable — factor in extra time. Keep some Turkish lira for last-minute tips and small purchases. Consider purchasing Turkish saffron, hand-painted tiles, or a quality Turkish towel (peshtemal) as final souvenirs.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport on flight UA at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome drink at the hotel bar, and enjoy a light late-night snack from room service.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Late-night room service — charcuterie board, Turkish mezze selection, and herbal tea upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer with the resort. Request early check-in amenities such as a turndown service, Turkish bath salts, and a welcome fruit basket. Keep the evening light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a lavish breakfast at the resort's sea-view restaurant. Afterward, take a private guided orientation tour of the Sultanahmet historic peninsula — visiting the exterior of the Blue Mosque, Hagia Sophia, and the Hippodrome to get your bearings in the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour inside the Topkapi Palace and its Imperial Treasury, including the Harem quarters. Explore the palace's stunning courtyards and collections of Ottoman artifacts, jewels, and sacred relics at a relaxed, unhurried pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's terrace overlooking the Bosphorus. Dinner at a premium waterfront restaurant in the Sultanahmet or Karaköy area.

meals.breakfast: Extravagant Turkish breakfast spread at the resort — simit, börek, clotted cream, honey, olives, sucuk, fresh cheeses, and seasonal fruits
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch at a traditional lokanta near Topkapi Palace — stuffed vine leaves, hummus, grilled eggplant, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mikla or a comparable rooftop fine-dining restaurant with panoramic Bosphorus views — modern Turkish cuisine with seasonal tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Book Topkapi Palace tickets in advance to skip queues. A private guide enhances the experience significantly. Dress modestly for mosque visits.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Hagia Sophia — one of the world's greatest architectural achievements. Explore its Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and layered history as a church, mosque, and museum. Follow with a visit to the nearby Basilica Cistern for an atmospheric underground experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive private tour of the Grand Bazaar — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets. With your guide, discover hidden artisan workshops, authentic carpet dealers, and curated shops for Ottoman antiques, hand-painted ceramics, and fine jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Turkish hammam experience at the historic Çemberlitaş Hamamı or the luxury Kılıç Ali Paşa Hamamı — full ritual bath, exfoliation, and oil massage. Return to the resort refreshed.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Havuzlu Restaurant inside the Grand Bazaar — a hidden gem serving classic Ottoman dishes in a courtyard setting
meals.dinner: Private dinner at Asitane Restaurant, renowned for recreating authentic Ottoman palace recipes from historical documents

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance, especially for the Kılıç Ali Paşa Hamamı which is highly sought after. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Grand Bazaar.

day_by_day.morning: Private Bosphorus yacht cruise departing from near the resort. Sail past the Dolmabahçe Palace, the Rumeli Fortress, and the Bosphorus Bridge. Enjoy champagne and fresh fruit on deck as you take in the stunning waterway that divides Europe and Asia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark on the Asian side of Istanbul — explore the charming Kadıköy neighborhood. Visit the vibrant Kadıköy Market for artisan produce, spices, and local street food. Browse the bohemian boutiques and antique shops of Moda.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the European side by private ferry. Rooftop cocktails in Karaköy, followed by dinner in the trendy Karaköy or Galata district.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on the private yacht — smoked salmon, pastries, fresh juice, and Turkish tea
meals.lunch: Street food exploration in Kadıköy Market — kokoreç, midye dolma (stuffed mussels), fresh fish sandwiches, and Turkish sweets
meals.dinner: Dinner at Neolokal — a celebrated Istanbul restaurant focusing on Anatolian heritage ingredients with a contemporary approach

day_by_day.notes: The private yacht can be arranged through the resort's concierge. The Asian side of Istanbul offers a completely different, more local atmosphere — a highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably Istanbul's most magnificent Ottoman mosque, offering sweeping views over the Golden Horn. Explore the surrounding historic neighborhood and the tomb of Suleiman the Magnificent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) with a private culinary guide. Sample Turkish spices, lokum (Turkish delight), dried fruits, and artisan products. Then take a private walking tour through the historic Eminönü and Balat neighborhoods — known for their colorful houses, Greek Orthodox churches, and synagogues.
day_by_day.evening: Private Turkish cooking class with a master chef — learn to prepare classic dishes such as stuffed peppers, lamb kebabs, and baklava. Enjoy the meal you've prepared as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional meyhane (Turkish tavern) in Balat — meze spread with rakı pairing
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the cooking class, paired with fine Turkish wines from the Thrace or Aegean regions

day_by_day.notes: The Balat neighborhood is photogenic and culturally rich — bring a camera. The cooking class can be arranged through the resort or a premium culinary tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Dolmabahçe Palace — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman imperial palace on the Bosphorus shore, featuring 285 rooms, 46 halls, and the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier. A stunning contrast to the older Topkapi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Nişantaşı neighborhood — Istanbul's answer to Paris's 16th arrondissement. Browse flagship Turkish designer boutiques, international luxury brands, and elegant patisseries. Visit the Istanbul Museum of Modern Art (Istanbul Modern) nearby in Beyoğlu.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk across or along the Galata Bridge. Visit the iconic Galata Tower for panoramic city views at dusk. Dinner in the lively Beyoğlu district.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at a Nişantaşı café — avocado toasts, artisan salads, and specialty coffee
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ulus 29 — a prestigious restaurant with breathtaking Bosphorus views and refined Turkish cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires pre-booked timed entry tickets. Istanbul Modern is one of Turkey's finest contemporary art spaces — worth 1–2 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private day trip to Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a private boat to Büyükada, the largest island. Explore the island by horse-drawn carriage (phaeton) or bicycle, visiting the historic Greek Orthodox monastery of St. George on the hilltop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on the peaceful island — swim at a private beach club, stroll through Victorian-era wooden mansions, and enjoy the car-free tranquility. Visit the island's charming town center for local crafts and ice cream.
day_by_day.evening: Return by private boat to Istanbul at sunset. Quiet evening at the resort — spa treatment, rooftop bar, and early dinner.

meals.breakfast: Packed gourmet breakfast prepared by the resort for the boat journey
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a waterfront restaurant on Büyükada — grilled sea bass, octopus salad, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant — tasting menu with Bosphorus views

day_by_day.notes: The Princes' Islands are a beloved escape from the city. May weather is ideal for this trip. Book the private boat through the resort concierge for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Chora Church (Kariye Museum) — home to some of the finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, recently restored. Located in the historic Edirnekapı neighborhood near the ancient Theodosian Walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the ancient Theodosian Land Walls of Constantinople — walk a section of these 5th-century walls with your private guide and understand their extraordinary historical significance. Continue to the Eyüp Sultan Mosque and cemetery, one of Istanbul's most sacred sites.
day_by_day.evening: Take the historic Pierre Loti cable car up to the famous Pierre Loti Café overlooking the Golden Horn for tea and views. Return for a special private dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional neighborhood lokanta in Eyüp — home-cooked Turkish dishes, lentil soup, and lamb stew
meals.dinner: Private in-suite dining experience at the resort — curated 5-course Ottoman tasting menu with sommelier-selected Turkish wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The Chora Church is a hidden gem often missed by tourists — a must for history and art lovers. The Eyüp area has a deeply spiritual atmosphere; dress respectfully.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Bursa — the first Ottoman capital, located across the Sea of Marmara. Take a private speedboat or ferry to Mudanya, then a private car to Bursa. Visit the magnificent Green Mosque (Yeşil Camii) and Green Tomb.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Bursa's Covered Bazaar (Kapalı Çarşı) and the historic Koza Han (Silk Cocoon Inn) — a stunning 15th-century caravanserai. Take the cable car up Uludağ mountain for panoramic views. Bursa is the birthplace of the İskender kebab.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private transfer and ferry. Relaxed evening at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Authentic İskender kebab lunch at Kebapçı İskender — the original restaurant where this iconic dish was invented, in Bursa
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at the resort's bar-restaurant — mezze platter and Turkish craft beer or wine

day_by_day.notes: Bursa is a UNESCO-recognized city and offers a completely different perspective on Ottoman history. The day trip is best arranged with a private driver and guide.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at leisure — enjoy the resort's spa, pool, or private beach. Optional yoga or wellness session arranged by the resort. Late, leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the Istanbul Archaeological Museums complex — three world-class museums in one: the Archaeological Museum with Alexander Sarcophagus, the Museum of the Ancient Orient, and the Tiled Kiosk Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail cruise on a private gulet (traditional wooden yacht) along the Bosphorus — watch the city's minarets and palaces glow in the golden hour light.

meals.breakfast: Extended brunch at the resort — eggs Benedict, fresh-squeezed juices, pastries, and premium Turkish cheeses
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the museum café or a nearby Sultanahmet restaurant
meals.dinner: Dinner on the private gulet — catered by a top Istanbul restaurant, served on deck under the stars

day_by_day.notes: A rest day mid-trip helps maintain energy for the remainder. The Archaeological Museums are underrated and house some of the most important artifacts in the world.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided exploration of the Beşiktaş and Ortaköy neighborhoods — vibrant, modern, and culturally rich areas along the Bosphorus. Visit the ornate Ortaköy Mosque set against the Bosphorus Bridge. Browse artisan weekend markets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sakıp Sabancı Museum in Emirgan — one of Istanbul's finest private art museums, set in a stunning Bosphorus villa. Features Ottoman calligraphy, paintings, and rotating international exhibitions. Stroll through the museum's garden café.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner at a top Istanbul restaurant — celebrate the journey with a special culinary experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Sakıp Sabancı Museum's Müzedechanga restaurant — innovative Turkish cuisine in a garden setting with Bosphorus views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sunset Grill & Bar — one of Istanbul's most prestigious restaurants with stunning Bosphorus panoramas and an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Ortaköy is famous for its kumpir (loaded baked potatoes) — try one as a street snack. The Sakıp Sabancı Museum garden is beautiful in May.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Rumeli Fortress (Rumelihisarı) — a dramatic 15th-century Ottoman castle built by Mehmed II before the conquest of Constantinople. Stunning Bosphorus views from the towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Bebek neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most exclusive waterfront areas. Stroll the promenade, visit artisan coffee shops, and browse independent boutiques. Optional visit to the Bosphorus University campus, one of the most scenic university grounds in the world.
day_by_day.evening: Final luxury hammam experience or resort spa treatment. Farewell dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — request a special table with the best Bosphorus view.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bebek Balıkçısı or a premium Bebek seafood restaurant — fresh catch of the day with Bosphorus views
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant — chef's special tasting menu with Turkish wine pairing and a personalized dessert

day_by_day.notes: Ask the resort to arrange a special farewell setup — champagne, flowers, or a personalized cake. Pack non-essential items this evening to ease the final morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at the resort — last swim, spa visit, or simply enjoy the Bosphorus views from the terrace. Final Turkish breakfast experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping or exploration near the hotel. Collect any pre-ordered items from artisan shops. Private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul. Reflect on an extraordinary 13-day journey through one of the world's most captivating cities.

meals.breakfast: Grand final Turkish breakfast at the resort — savor every last bite of simit, fresh honey, clotted cream, and çay (Turkish tea)
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort or airport's premium lounge
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the transfer and Istanbul Airport check-in procedures. The resort concierge can arrange a private luxury transfer. Consider purchasing authentic Turkish delights, saffron, hand-painted ceramics, or a small carpet as final souvenirs.
